court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court No.3, Mumbai in Petition No.A.1270/2011
case_name: Smt. Kusumlata Raj Kumar Sureka vs Mr. Mahendra Sureka And Anr
facts_of_case: Petitioner Kusumlata Rajkumar Sureka sought impleadment in a petition filed by her husband Mahendra Sureka against his wife Sarika under Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 for dissolution of marriage on grounds of cruelty and desertion. The trial court allowed an application by Sarika to hand over keys of the suit premises.

legal_principles.principle: A respondent's statement on instructions from the respondent, made in court, can be binding.
legal_principles.held: We dispose of the Civil Application by accepting the statement made on behalf of the respondent, that would be binding on the respondent.

legal_principles.principle: A court can restrain a party from dispossessing another party from a property till the first party makes alternate arrangements.
legal_principles.held: The learned trial Judge restrained Kusumlata and Mahendra from dispossessing Sarika from the suit premises till Mahendra makes alternate arrangement for accommodation for Sarika to her satisfaction within a period of six months.

outcome.final_order: The final order recalled the earlier order directing Mahendra Sureka to provide a set of keys of the main door of the suit premises to Sarika.
